domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
in the definition of H_n, k ranges over integers from 1 to n
in the definition of f_n(x), x is a real number so that floor(n*x) and floor(k*x) are well-defined
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every natural number n greater than 1, define H_n as the sum from k = 1 to n of 1 divided by k, and define f_n on real numbers by f_n(x) = floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (floor of k times x) divided by k. Then for every real number r with (n minus 1) divided by n less than or equal to r and r less than 1, it holds that f_n(r) equals H_n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all natural numbers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with (n-1)/n <= r and r < 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: parameter for the definitions of H_n and f_n; also bounds the index set for k

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index running from 1 to n

variables.name: x
variables.role: argument of the function f_n used in its definition

variables.name: r
variables.role: input at which the equality f_n(r) = H_n - 1 is asserted

variables.name: f_n
variables.role: function defined from n, using floor and a weighted sum

witness_dependencies: no existential witnesses are introduced; the statement is a universal implication from the condition on r to the equality

statement_nl: Let n > 1, define H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, and let f_n be defined by f_n(x) = floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k. If r is a real number with (n-1)/n <= r < 1, then f_n(r) = H_n - 1.
